ai.description: The Marbled Toad (Bufonidae) grows to 8 cm. It features a grey-brown body with irregular dark marbling and a pale vertebral stripe. A prominent, continuous bony ridge above each eye is diagnostic.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Firouzophrynus stomaticus* is the presence of a distinct, pale, glandular ridge (tarsal fold) along the inner edge of the foot.
ai.habitat: The Marbled Toad inhabits diverse environments, ranging from arid scrublands and grasslands to agricultural fields, typically at elevations below 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Marbled Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects and small invertebrates while remaining inactive in burrows during the heat of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Marbled Toad is an oviparous breeder that lays large, gelatinous egg strings in temporary monsoon pools. Breeding occurs during the rainy season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Marbled Toad is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the arid plains of Pakistan and North India to elevations of 2,500 meters in the Himalayas.
ai.callDescription: The Marbled Toad produces a high-pitched, rhythmic "trill" or "chirp" repeated at short intervals, typically heard near temporary rain pools or water bodies after monsoon rains.
